If any axis shows disjoint intervals ($min_1 \ge max_2$ or $min_2 \ge max_1$), return `false`; else return `true` [S2, unofficial].

The claim accurately describes the Separating Axis Theorem (SAT) logic for triangle intersection as detailed in the 'Source [S2] notes'. Specifically, the notes state: 'If any axis shows disjoint intervals (`min1 >= max2 || min2 >= max1`), return 0 (no intersection). Else return 1 (intersection).' The claim maps 'return 0' to `false` and 'return 1' to `true`, which is a standard logical interpretation of the boolean result for intersection checks. All factual components of the claim (the condition for disjoint intervals and the resulting return values) are present in the evidence.
